evals.name: add-property-with-sources-and-fixtures
evals.prompt: Screenplay MCP 4.142.0 has our scratch model open. RegisterProject produces ProjectRegistered, which AutoMaps into ProjectSummary; specifications and examples already cover this chain. Add a required String priority to all three, using literal normal in existing fixtures. ProjectRegistered has persisted events; the planner returned EventContractChangeRequiresDecision without an event mode. Can the catalog justify eventNeverPersisted or an AST bypass? List the tool calls and arguments without executing or writing files. Include what you do if mapping sources or fixtures are missing, a hop is off-chain, or a nested feed is unsupported. We keep comments in the model.
evals.expected_output: Inspect existing producer/consumer property references and dependencies with revision paging, then read owner and mapping handles. Use propose-property action add, both revision guards, owner, expectedOwnerName, name, type, optional false, declaration hops {at,name}, mapping hops {at,value}, fixtureValue literal source text and newGeneration true. A catalog proves no storage history, so do not claim eventNeverPersisted or bypass EventContractChangeRequiresDecision with AST/text; N+1 preserves history and requires transformation before deployment. Exactly one mode applies to selected events; both true is invalid. Same-named AutoMap can satisfy the read-model hop. Missing sources/value refuse SourcesRequired/FixtureValueRequired, off-chain HopNotOnChain, nested feeds UnsupportedPropertySpan. Required additions populate existing fixtures/assertions; optional additions do not. Review property decisions, chainCandidates, generations, bytes, dropped comments and semantic diff; run specifications on the proposal. Only a reviewed apply writes. Never compose an AST batch to bypass the planner.
assertions: Looks up existing chain evidence before changing it and treats incomplete evidence as a limitation, not a safe empty list.
Uses propose-property action add, both revisions, owner, expectedOwnerName, name, type and optional false rather than a hand-composed propose-ast batch.
Distinguishes declaration hops {at,name} from mapping hops {at,value}; recognizes same-named AutoMap as a compatible source, not permission to guess expressions.

Provides fixtureValue as literal source text, explains required versus optional fixture handling, and names SourcesRequired, FixtureValueRequired, HopNotOnChain and UnsupportedPropertySpan without bypassing them.

Selects newGeneration for the persisted event, never infers non-persistence from catalog state or bypasses EventContractChangeRequiresDecision with AST/text, requires transformation before deployment and CanonicalizeTouchedDocuments, reviews comments/generations/semantic diff, and runs proposal specs before apply.

evals.name: rename-command-input-without-renaming-payload
evals.prompt: Through Screenplay MCP 4.142.0, rename only RegisterProject.title to displayName. ProjectRegistered.title and ProjectSummary.title must keep their names. Explain the chain lookup, proposal arguments, review, and how to handle StaleRevision at apply. Do not execute calls or edit files.
evals.expected_output: Read Property references/dependencies with pinned sourceRevision, inspect incomplete and ambiguous rows, and obtain original property handles. propose-property action rename with target, expectedName title, newName displayName and workspace/catalog revision guards, without alsoRename for unselected fields. Mappings/fixtures are repaired, event payload names remain unchanged, broken AutoMap gets an explicit mapping. Review needsDecision, chainCandidates, notChanged, bytes and semantic diff. StaleRevision requires reopening, inspecting drift and re-proposing, never retrying unchanged or text-editing.
assertions: Inspects kind Property evidence and direct counterparts, pages with expectedSourceRevision and does not assume incomplete means no references.
Uses propose-property action rename with target, expectedName, newName and both revisions, not a hand-composed AST batch.
Leaves unselected event/read-model properties unchanged, explains mapping and fixture repair and AutoMap preservation, and treats chainCandidates as unselected evidence.
Reviews the retained proposal and semantic diff before apply, and reopens/re-proposes after StaleRevision rather than forcing the old proposal or editing text.

evals.name: read-generation-support-and-rule-proofs
evals.prompt: Screenplay MCP 4.173.0 has Shop open. InvoiceNumber uses a date pattern with checksum; another concept uses an Int64 random range; a third has generate rule TenantOrder. declaration-details returns generation.arguments, exact supportCount beyond JavaScript safe integer, entropyBits, derivedPattern and rules[]. One rule is refuted with witness and repair PLAY0688; an unused uuid concept is refuted without diagnosticCode; another rule is unproven. Explain inspection, adding a matches rule and replacing the refuted rule, without executing edits. Is empty executable.diagnosticCodes admission?
evals.expected_output: Read kind Concept/view summary generation.arguments (not previewArguments): pattern/checksum/rule strings or range text with exact Int64 endpoints; preserve raw supportCount, entropyBits log2 support, dates use minimum conditioned support and checksums add no entropy. Opaque rule entropy is unknown; inspect ValueGeneration implementation-requirements, never run the body. Read authored-order rules status/witness/reason, not diagnostic prose. Add a rule through typed ConceptSyntax proposal using derivedPattern, preserve other members and review input/stored-value changes. Replace refuted rules only through discovered PLAY0688 subject/propose-repair with both revisions and canonical formatting; checksum pattern repair may also add missing checksum validation. Refuted without diagnosticCode means compiler did not check it, so no repair is reported. Null derivedPattern needs its reason, not fabrication; Unproven isn't proof. Review, run candidate specs, then apply. Admission requires whole-model executable.status admitted, not empty local codes.
assertions: Reads generation.arguments, exact range endpoints/supportCount without floating-point rounding, distinguishes entropy estimates and unknown opaque-rule entropy, and does not parse diagnostics for rule status.
Uses authored-order rules[].status, witness/reason and conditional diagnosticCode/repair; explains refuted without diagnosticCode as compiler-not-checked and does not invent a repair.

Uses derivedPattern through a typed matches proposal to add a rule and discovered PLAY0688 propose-repair with both revisions/canonical formatting to replace one, reviewing checksum additions and input/stored-value consequences.
Distinguishes null derivedPattern/reason and Unproven from proof or admission, and requires whole-model admitted status rather than empty diagnosticCodes.
Inspects ValueGeneration requirements for an opaque rule, reviews candidate changes and runs proposal specifications before apply; never executes attached generation code through MCP.

evals.name: compare-active-model-with-main-worktree
evals.prompt: What changed in my model compared with main? Screenplay MCP 4.131.0 already has /work/repo/Screenplay open. A registered worktree checked out at main has the baseline in /work/repo-main/Screenplay. Give the comparison call and explain paging if either model changes, whether this writes anything, and which tool to use instead for an unapplied proposal. Do not export both models or change files.
evals.expected_output: Call semantic-diff with before: { path: '/work/repo-main/Screenplay' } and after: { workspace: 'active' }, using the corresponding model folder after verifying the baseline checkout. No exports or Git-ref resolution are needed. It reads without writing and refuses pending interrupted writes. Repeat the selections and echo sourceRevision as expectedSourceRevision on continuation; both sides reload and changed revisions refuse as StaleRevision, requiring a fresh comparison. Use read-proposal view=semantic-diff for a retained proposal against disk. Neither is behavioral execution evidence.
assertions: Uses semantic-diff with a before path source for /work/repo-main/Screenplay and an after workspace active source, not two exports or a Git ref.
Verifies the worktree baseline and states the comparison is read-only, with pending interrupted writes refused.
Echoes the pair-bound sourceRevision as expectedSourceRevision on continuation with the same source selections, and restarts after StaleRevision because both sides reload.
Uses read-proposal view=semantic-diff for an unapplied proposal against disk and distinguishes structural comparison from execution evidence.

evals.name: record-and-resolve-question-note
evals.prompt: Screenplay MCP 4.144.0 has Library.Loans.CheckIn open. We have not decided whether a member can cancel after check-in; assume no cancellation for now. Record a question note, citing our project decision register entry D123, then explain how to resolve it when D123 rules out cancellation. Show tool-call arguments and the review/apply loop, but do not execute calls or write files. A source removal proposal reports this note in orphanedNotes; also explain that review, what null orphanedNotes means, and whether cratis CLI 3.53.1 can fail on questions. Use a team-role author and no personal data.
evals.expected_output: Open/read current workspace, catalog and notes state; list bounded notes by address/kind or semanticId, scope, kind question, state all, and ref D123 as appropriate, pinning notesRevision on continuation. Propose-model-notes with expectedRevision, expectedCatalogRevision, expectedNotesRevision and operations add: kind question, text with consequence/assumption, author modeling-team, exactly target address/kind or a real catalog anchor, refs [{id:D123}]. The server supplies note ID/time. Review read-proposal view notes, pin afterNotesRevision on review continuation, then apply with ordinary proposal ID and before workspace/catalog revisions; no notes argument on apply. Reread after apply and use returned ID in a resolve operation whose resolution has by external-decision, ref {id:D123}, text and author; review then apply again. Resolve is not implementation: carry cancellation rule into model/specification, clarified description or a durable project decision record. Review source orphan IDs before apply; reanchor to a surviving element or resolve with evidence and retain orphan history explicitly; resolution does not fix anchor. Separate notes apply means re-propose source. Null/unreadable impact is unknown, never empty; do not auto-repair unreadable notes. Notes sidecar is committed, no secrets/personal data; notes do not change ESM/compilation. Model-note.open-question is MCP/CLI only, no PLAY code. Standalone Screenplay 4.144.0 supports open-questions fail (1 for selected open questions, 2 unreadable); cratis CLI 3.53.1 does not. Warnaserror alone ignores notes.
assertions: Records an anchored committed question note, not chat/description, with assumption/consequence and no secrets/personal data; lists relevant filters including state all for orphans and pins expectedNotesRevision on continuation.
Uses propose-model-notes operations add with kind, text, team author, exactly one anchor/target and refs D123, all three revision guards, and server-generated IDs/timestamps.

Reviews read-proposal view notes with afterNotesRevision on continuation; applies only the reviewed proposal with ordinary before workspace/catalog guards and no extra notes argument; rereads state for resolution.

Resolves with by external-decision, required ref D123, explanation and author, then realizes the answer in a specification/description/decision record; reviews orphanedNotes before source apply, treats null/unreadable as unknown, distinguishes resolving from reanchoring and re-proposes source after notes apply.

Names model-note.open-question as info MCP/CLI-only with no PLAY code, separates it from ESM/V1 and warns that notes are committed; standalone 4.144.0 has the fail gate but cratis CLI 3.53.1 does not.
